newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to launch "electrical appliances capital".
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to launch "electrical appliances capital".

text.p: Malaysia will launch an industrial town on Monday devoted to producing locally-made electrical appliances in another government push to improve the country's trade balance.
The four-billion ringgit ($1.6 billion) project, called MEC City, will be launched by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
Products from MEC City, already billed as the country's "electrical appliances capital", will be sold domestically and abroad.
A brainchild of Mahathir's, the project is part of government efforts to shrink a worrisome current account deficit by eventually reducing the country's need for certain imports.

Malaysia is also seeking investment in its "Multimedia Super Corridor", a 15- by 50-km (nine by 30 mile) zone stretching south from Kuala Lumpur to where a new airport and federal capital are under construction.
The government aims to attract world class information technology firms to the zone, from satellite education providers to software designers and electronic publishers.
"It should be viewed as a long-term positive development," said Nik Fauzan, an economist at Vickers Ballas Research in Kuala Lumpur, of MEC City.
"Initially, you need to import equipment for the project. But in the long run, it would ease a lot of imports and thus lessen the burden on the current account," he said.
Consumer goods account for about 50 percent of Malaysia's total imports.

Malaysia posted a trade deficit of 617.97 million ringgit in 1996, against a 9.36 billion gap in 1995. The deficit is widely expected to narrow further over 1997, but at a slower pace due to infrastructure projects which need imports, analysts said.
The current account, measuring trade in services as well as merchandise, was officially projected to level off at a deficit of 11.45 billion ringgit in 1997, about the same as in 1996.
An analyst with a foreign brokerage house said the project was part of a growing process as Malaysia aims to be an industrialised nation by 2020.
"Given the success of (national car) Proton, people will be less critical about national projects now," he said. "But of course, there'll be tough competition."
Malaysian-made products will be competing with foreign imported goods which will be enjoying lower tariffs by 1998 under international trade agreements, the analyst said.
Malaysia's electrical appliances market is currently dominated by established Japanese and South Korean products.
MEC City is sited on 1,200 hectares (2,965 acres) of land near Kuantan city on the east coast with the entire project due to be fully developed in 10 years.

Malaysia Electric Corp Bhd (MEC), a wholly-owned unit of property and manufacturing firm Kuala Lumpur Industries Holdings Bhd, will lead the project. MEC has been producing electrical appliances for the last 20 years.

MEC will eventually make products like rice cookers, kettles, televisions, air-conditioners and refrigerators under the MEC brand. Company officials said MEC hopes to export 70 percent of its products to various markets in three years.

On Friday, MEC signed an agreement for the distribution of its products in Burma. It has also also secured a contract worth $500 million to supply electrical products to the United Arab Emirates, officials said.
($1 = 2.48 ringgit)
